newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE SEEN STABILISING AFTER CURRENT FALL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE SEEN STABILISING AFTER CURRENT FALL.

text.p: The Polish bourse was seen stabilising next week after this week's 3.3-percent fall but analysts were split on whether the market would soon extend its recent surge or slip more.

"The market should rebound around Tuesday and then...it will be easier to say if there'll be a continuation of the recent rises in the mid-term or more of a flat trend," said Tomasz Cwintal of Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.
The main WIG index closed at 17,543.8 points on Friday.

Some analysts said Wednesday's perceived bearish statements by U.S Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan could slow foreign buying, which had been credited for spurring the bourse's 38-percent surge from mid-December to February 18.

They said Friday's news that food prices in February's second ten days rose by only 0.1 percent was a good sign which could help the market mood even though no immediate interest rate cut was expected.
"It (low mid-February food prices) suggests the expectations of two-percent inflation in February are realistic," said Wojciech Bialek of Magnus brokerage.
Analysts said investors would be watching next week to see if small-cap stocks continue this week's outperformance of high-capitalised issues.
Espebepe rose 30.6 percent this week, despite Friday's 9.8-percent profit-taking correction after speculation it would win a debt write-off deal in mid March.
Prochnik rose 21.1 percent, buoyed by the public tender offer by 9.9-percent owner National Investment Fund No. 12 to increase its stake to 32.9 percent at a premium to the market price.
But a similar tender offer by Denmark's NKT Cables' to buy up Kable shares at a discount depressed the stock's price by 9.8 percent on Friday.
Analysts said stocks would likely not suffer from next week's primary-market offers, which see the end of the 500,000-share retail tranche at 65 zlotys per share of drug maker on Friday.
On Monday road builder starts trade on the bourse's main market.
